school.tagged_body:
My uncle was watching a rocket video. His girlfriend came into the room.

"Why are you watching that again?" she asked.

"I want to know. Can the rocket really fly?" he said.

She laughed. "Next time, send your money to space with it."

My uncle almost laughed. "I'm {{v:serious}}. I lost a lot of money."

"I know," she said. "That's why I'm making jokes. You look {{v:sad}} these days."

Then she sat next to him.

"{{t:You feel bad, and that is normal}}. But one bad choice will not {{v:ruin}} your life," she said.

My uncle {{v:nodded}} slowly. "{{g:Do you think things will get better?|미래시제(will) 의문문: 앞으로 일어날 일을 물어보는 표현}}" he asked.

"I don't know," she said. "{{g:But do not worry all day|명령문(Do not ~): '~하지 마라'는 부정 명령}}. {{g:It will not help|미래시제(will) 부정문: '~하지 않을 것이다'}}."

{{t:That evening, they watched the rocket launch together}}. My uncle {{v:enjoyed}} it, and he did not think about money.

One evening, my uncle was watching a SpaceX rocket video {{g:when his girlfriend walked into the room|시간 부사절(when + 주어 + 동사): '~할 때'}}.

"Why are you watching that again?" she asked.

"I'm {{g:checking if their rockets can really fly|명사절 if(간접의문문): '~인지 아닌지'를 나타내는 목적어절}}," he answered.

She laughed. "Next time, you should ask them to take your {{v:investment}} into space with them."

My uncle tried not to laugh because the joke was a little too true. "I'm {{v:serious}}. I lost a lot of money."

"I know," she said. "That's why I'm making jokes. You look {{v:unhappy}} these days, and I don't like it."

Then she sat down next to him.

"{{g:It is normal to feel bad|가주어 It + to부정사(진주어): 'It'은 형식상 주어, 'to feel bad'가 진짜 주어}} when things do not go as {{v:planned}}," she said {{v:gently}}. "But {{t:one bad investment does not decide your whole future}}."

My uncle nodded slowly. "Do you really think things will get better?" he asked.

"I don't know," she answered {{v:honestly}}. "But I do know that {{g:worrying all day won't make them better|동명사 주어(Worrying all day) + make + 목적어 + 형용사: '~가 …하게 만들다'}}."

{{t:That evening, they watched the rocket launch together}}. For the first time in days, my uncle enjoyed it {{g:instead of thinking only about money|전치사 instead of + 동명사(thinking): '~하는 대신에'}}.

My uncle was replaying a SpaceX rocket video when his girlfriend walked in. {{g:From the way he stared at the screen, it was clear that|it is clear that + 명사절: '~라는 것이 분명했다', 문맥으로 심리 상태를 드러내는 구문}} he was looking for something more than entertainment.

"I'm checking {{g:whether their rockets can actually make it up there|whether+주어+동사: '~인지 아닌지'를 나타내는 명사절(간접의문문)}}," he answered, {{g:although he already knew the answer|양보의 접속사 although: '비록 ~이지만'}}.

He nodded slowly, {{g:as if he was trying to decide whether he could believe her|as if + 절: 실제와 다른 상태를 가정하는 표현 + 명사절 whether}}. "Do you really think things will get better?" he asked.

That evening, they watched the rocket launch together, and for the first time in days, my uncle enjoyed it {{v:instead}} of thinking only about {{v:his losses}}.
